subject: Geofence commitments & cross-border processing clarifications
thread_content:
From: Emily Sandoval <emily.sandoval@acera.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Patrick Lewis <patrick.lewis@acera.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Geofence commitments for EU data + quick questions on backups

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, legal and security have a few specific asks so we can sign the DPA and confirm technical design. High level: Acera needs an explicit written commitment that EU customer workloads and PII will be pinned to the EU, including during normal operation and planned maintenance. We also need clarity on cross-region processing for things like audits, backups, and analytics.

Our immediate questions:
- When an EU workspace is configured to be EU-pinned, are any tokens/requests ever routed to non-EU compute for inference or preprocessing?
- How do you handle backups/snapshots — are they stored only in the EU region or are they replicated outside the EU for DR?
- Are audit logs or telemetry exported to Redwood central services in the US for operational monitoring?
- Can you provide the latest subprocessor list and indicate which subprocessors have access to customer data and where they are located?

We attached the DPA template our counsel provided for redlines. Can your legal/ops teams confirm which clauses you can accept and which need discussion? Also: we prefer a short diagram showing your geo-failover behavior for EU workloads.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Sandoval
Director, Product Security — Acera Health
emily.sandoval@acera.com

--
Attachment: Acera_DPA_v1_for_redwood.pdf (application/pdf)

-----Original Message-----
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sandoval <emily.sandoval@acera.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Geofence commitments for EU data + quick questions on backups

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary while I pull people in:

- Short answer: yes, we can commit to EU pinning for production inference and persistent customer data when a customer elects EU residency. That includes model input/output storage and key backups.
- Backups/DR: by default, snapshots for EU-pinned workspaces remain in the EU region. We offer an opt-in cross-region DR program that replicates snapshots to a customer-specified region; that is only enabled with explicit contractual consent and is logged in the Console.
- Operational telemetry & logs: aggregated metrics used for platform health are sent to Redwood control plane endpoints. For EU-pinned customers we offer a private control plane option (Redwood Private) where logs remain in the EU; for Hosted customers we can provide contractual limitations and a logging partitioning commitment to minimize exported telemetry.
- Subprocessors: attaching our latest subprocessor list. Kimberly will confirm access scopes and any EU-based subprocessors.

I'm looping in Kimberly (security) and Marissa (legal/contracts) to confirm precise DPA language. Hannah, could you attach a short geo-failover diagram and confirm if there are any rare maintenance cases where non-EU compute is used for short-lived tasks?

Next steps: Marissa to propose DPA redlines; Kimberly to annotate subprocessors; Hannah to add diagram. Can we aim to return a consolidated reply by EOD Wed?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

--
Attachments: (none in this message)

-----Original Message-----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sandoval <emily.sandoval@acera.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:45:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Geofence commitments for EU data + quick questions on backups

Hi Emily — thanks for the questions. I attached the current subprocessor export (CSV) and added a short note in the Spreadsheet about access levels. Quick answers inline: 

- Inference routing: for EU-pinned workspaces the serving runtime is pinned to EU-hosted GPU pools; ephemeral helpers (e.g., model compilation jobs, certain internal offline evals) will not run in non-EU regions unless the customer has enabled cross-region DR or has a deployment that spans regions. Any exception requires customer consent and is logged.
- Backups/snapshots: by default stored in EU object storage (within the selected EU region). Cross-region replication is opt-in and cannot be toggled by Redwood for a pinned workspace without a signed workflow (DocuSign/contract amendment).
- Audit logs: application-level audit logs for EU-pinned customers are retained in the EU. Platform-level telemetry (high-level metrics) is sent to our central monitoring; we can provide a telemetry partitioning commitment and an exportable logs bundle on-demand for compliance audits.

I flagged two DPA points that will likely need negotiation: (1) the ‘universal access’ clause that allows Redwood staff to access data for troubleshooting — we propose restricting that to named support roles and audited sessions; (2) the DR replication clause — we want to keep an opt-in model rather than a hard prohibition on certain technical options. Marissa will propose contract language.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

--

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sandoval <emily.sandoval@acera.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geofence commitments for EU data + quick questions on backups

Hi Emily — attached is a redlined DPA (DPA_v3_redlined.pdf) with our proposed edits. Summary of key changes:

1) Data residency clause: we added an explicit definition for ‘EU residency’ and committed to region pinning for production inference, persistent customer-stored artifacts, and backups unless cross-region DR is explicitly enabled by contract.
2) Access controls: we narrowed the support access clause and added requirements for Just-In-Time access, audited sessions, and customer notification for high-sensitivity incidents.
3) Subprocessors: we accepted a requirement to notify Acera of material changes and to provide quarterly exportable records of subprocessors touching EU data.

Hannah attached a geo-failover diagram showing the default behavior: 
- Primary: EU GPUS & object store
- Local snapshots retained in EU
- Optional: DR replication to customer-approved region (requires contract addendum)

If these redlines are acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope. Otherwise please highlight any clauses you need to re-open.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
Attachments: DPA_v3_redlined.pdf (application/pdf), geo-failover-diagram.png (image/png)

Marissa / Sofia — thanks for the thorough reply and the redlines. This looks promising. A few follow-ups from legal: 
- Can you add a clause that requires Redwood to give 30 days’ notice before enabling any cross-region DR for an EU-pinned tenant (even if opt-in)?
- For access controls, can we get an exportable list of named people who might be granted Just-In-Time access for support (or an approval workflow)?
- For telemetry partitioning, can you confirm the retention period for platform-level metrics that may be stored outside the EU?

If you can accept the 30-day notice for DR and provide the support-person export or workflow, we are comfortable moving to DocuSign. Please send the envelope when ready.

Emily
Emily Sandoval
Director, Product Security — Acera Health
